title: Home to Talwandi
hookLine: tradition says his parents begged Nanak to stay; he told them his work was on the road

cards: The airport arrivals hall. A mother on her toes behind the barrier, scanning faces. A father pretending to be calm, holding the car keys too tight.
And then the one they've waited for walks through, and for a few minutes nobody can speak. Plenty of families who have sent someone far away know that hall.
In the janamsakhis, Guru Nanak's parents get their arrivals hall too, on the edge of their own village. And the hardest part comes after the hug. Today: Talwandi.

teach.h: THE VILLAGE WHERE HE WAS BORN.
teach.b: Talwandi was the village where Nanak was born, where, tradition says, his father, Mehta Kalu, kept the village accounts, and his mother, Mata Tripta, raised him.

In the tellings, after a long stretch of travel, Nanak and Mardana come back toward it. Some tellings keep a detail: Nanak doesn't walk straight in. He stops outside the village and sends Mardana ahead.
Word reaches the house. His mother comes running out to find him; his father follows. Tradition says they wept, and held him, and then they begged.
Stay. Rest. Take up a life here, among your people.
We've waited long enough. And Nanak, in the tellings, answers with love, and doesn't move.

teach.h: STAY. HIS WORK IS ON THE ROAD.
teach.b: His work, he tells them, is on the road. What does this story know?

teach.h: LOVE ON BOTH SIDES OF THE CALL.
teach.b: That a call can pull against the people you love most, and that the pull is real on both sides. The parents aren't villains; their begging is a natural thing. And Nanak's answer isn't coldness.
The Guru Granth Sahib uses the language of family to speak of God, calling the Divine mother and father, kin and brother. A path that prays like that has not stopped honoring parents.
Nanak has been called elsewhere, and he goes with his parents' tears still on his shoulder.
And notice where the larger story ends up: after the journeys, Nanak settles at Kartarpur as a householder, with family around him. The road didn't swallow the home forever.
But on this day at Talwandi, it had to come first.

how: Sikhs tell the sakhi of Guru Nanak's return to Talwandi, his birthplace, now Nankana Sahib, as a story of love for family held together with the call to travel and teach.

games.q: you're Nanak, back at the edge of your birth village. your mother and father hold you and beg you to stay. what do you do?
o: stay, and take up village life.
answer with love, and keep to the road.
slip away before dawn without a word.
games.why: tradition says Nanak told them his work was on the road. the story keeps the love on both sides, and the larger story ends with him settled at Kartarpur among family.

practice: Bring to mind whoever waited for your arrivals: a parent, a grandparent, an aunt, a teacher, an older neighbor.

If they're gone, see their face and remember one thing they used to say; if they're here, simply hold them in mind for a while and let yourself be glad of them. If you pray, you can say Waheguru with them in mind.
